paper.title_en: Topological graviton mass generation and Chern-Simons graviton scattering amplitudes
paper.abstract_en: We study the mechanism of topological mass generation in 3d topologically massive gravity (TMG). We establish a Topological Graviton Equivalence Theorem (TGRET) to uncover this mechanism. We formulate TMG in Weyl-transformed variables by introducing a compensating (unphysical) dilaton field that decouples in unitary gauge. In the Weyl-transformed TMG (WTMG), the massive graviton has one physical degree of freedom, which will be transferred to the dilaton field in the massless limit. We present the BRST quantization of the WTMG and prove the TGRET to all loop orders for the first time. The TGRET connects each N-point graviton scattering amplitude to the dilaton amplitude in the high-energy limit. Using the TGRET, we prove in general that the N-point Chern-Simons graviton amplitudes (N ≥ 4) have striking high-energy cancellations that ensure good ultraviolet behavior. In particular, the four-point and five-point graviton amplitudes respectively exhibit substantial high-energy cancellations at tree level, E<sup loc="post">12</sup> → E<sup loc="post">1</sup> and E<sup loc="post">15</sup> → E<sup loc="post">0</sup>, in TMG.
